To Gershon belonged Ladan and Shimei.
The sons of Ladan: Nahnael, the eldest, Jotham, and Joel—three.
The sons of Shemaiah: Shelomoth, Hazael, and Aran—three. These were the heads of the ancestral households of Shimei.
The sons of Shimei: Nahath, Zabida, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the four sons of Shimei.
Nahath was the eldest, Zebidah the second, and then Jeush and Beriah. Beriah did not have many sons, and they formed one clan within their ancestral household.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four.

The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was chosen, together with his sons forever, to minister in the Holy of Holies, to offer fragrant incense before the LORD, to serve him, and to bless in his name forever.
Moses, the prophet of the Lord, was reckoned as belonging to the tribe of the house of Levi.
The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
The sons of Gershom: Samuel, his eldest.
The sons of Eliezer: Rahmiah, the eldest. Eliezer had no other sons. The sons of Rahmiah: Ribi, the eldest.
The sons of Izhar: Shelomoth, his eldest.
The sons of Hebron: Judah, the eldest, Amariah the second, Nahaziel the third, and Nekamaim the fourth.
The sons of Uzziel: Micah, the eldest, and Shuah the second.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without sons, having only daughters, and the sons of Kish, their uncle, married them.
The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jarmun—three.

These were the sons of Levi according to their ancestral houses, the heads of ancestral families, counted individually by name. They were responsible for the work required in the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upward.
For David said, “The Lord of lords has given rest to his people Israel, and he dwells in Jerusalem from now on and forever.”
Those Levites are also to carry the tabernacle and all the equipment used for its service.
For according to David’s final instructions, the census of the descendants of Levi was completed, counting those twenty years old and upward.

For he appointed them alongside the sons of Aaron to have authority in the house of the Lord over those who sounded the straight and curved horns, and over the chests in which the Lord’s sacred vessels were stored.
And for the bread of the Presence, the fine flour, the unleavened cakes, and all those who offer praise and thanksgiving.
They were to stand every morning to thank and praise the Lord, and likewise every evening.
They were also to offer burnt offerings to the Lord on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the festivals, in the numbers required of them, regularly before the Lord.

They were to take charge of the tabernacle’s utensils and the sacred vessels, and to carry out the duties assigned by their brothers, the sons of Aaron, whenever they were required to serve in the house of the Lord.
As for Aaron’s sons, these were their divisions. Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died during the lifetime of their father Aaron, and they had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David, together with Zadok from the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their numbers and their responsibilities.

When counted individually, the sons of Eleazar were found to be more numerous than the sons of Ithamar. He divided them by individuals and ancestral houses: the sons of Eleazar numbered sixteen, and the sons of Ithamar, counted individually according to their ancestral houses, numbered eight.
He divided them by lot, one group alongside the other, because there were leaders of the sanctuary and rulers of the priests among both the sons of Eleazar and the sons of Ithamar.

Shemaiah son of Methlael, a scribe from the Levites, recorded them before King David, the elders of Israel, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the ancestral families of the priests and Levites. The first ancestral house was one from Eleazar, and the next one was from Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiada, and the second to Jedaiah.
The third to Hadam, and the fourth to Seorim.
The fifth to Malchijah, and the sixth to Mamin.
The seventh to Hakkoz, and the eighth to Abijah.
The ninth to Elisha, and the tenth to Shecaniah.
The eleventh to Elisha, and the twelfth to Eliakib.
The thirteenth to Huppah, and the fourteenth to Hadiah.
The fifteenth to Bilgah, and the sixteenth to Immer.
The seventeenth to Ahaziah, and the eighteenth to Pazzin.
The nineteenth to Pethahiah, and the twentieth to Ezekiel.
The twenty-first to Nekannam, and the twenty-second to Gamul.
The twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maadiah.

These were their numbered divisions for their duties when entering the house of the Lord, according to their regulations and what was required of them under the direction of their father Aaron, as the Lord of lords of Israel had commanded.
As for the remaining sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shobal; of the sons of Shobal, Jehdeiah.
And Rehabiah; of the sons of Rehabiah, Shua, his eldest.
And Izhar and Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Nahath.
And Jeremiah, Hazael, and Nekameam.
The sons of Hazael: Micah. For the sons of Micah: Shamir.
And Jeshua; of the sons of Jeshua, Zechariah.
The sons of Uzzim: his son.
These are the sons of Levi, according to their ancestral houses.

They too cast lots alongside their brothers and the sons of Aaron, before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the ancestral families of the priests and Levites. In the reckoning and the count, the younger was counted just like his older brother.
This was the number of the men who carried out the work in their assigned duties.
The sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Israel. These sons of Asaph were the ones whom the king appointed.

For Jeduthun, in the songs of praise: the sons of Jeduthun were Azariah, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, Mattithiah, and Jeduthun—six. These were entrusted to their father Jeduthun to sing praises with lyres and give thanks to the Lord.
And from the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shobal, Jeremoth, and Hananiah.
They were counted together with their brothers, and they sang songs of praise to the Lord. The number of these singers was two hundred and eighty-eight.
The younger was counted just like the older, and the pupil just like the teacher.
The first lot fell to Asaph, to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah—he, his brothers, and his sons, twelve.
The third to Zeuri—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fourth to Nizri—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The fifth to Nethaniah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The sixth to Bukkiah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The seventh to Sariel—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eighth to Isaiah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The ninth to Mattaniah—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The tenth to Shimeali—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The eleventh to Uzziel—his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The twelfth: Hashabiah, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The thirteenth: Shubael, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The fourteenth: Mattithiah, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The fifteenth: Jeremoth, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The sixteenth: Hananiah, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The seventeenth: Eliashib, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The eighteenth: Hanani, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The nineteenth: Mallothi, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The twentieth: Eliab, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The twenty-first: Jether, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The twenty-second: Jarib, his sons, and his brothers—twelve.
The division of the gates for which King David appointed guards: Meshelemiah, from the descendants of Joseph.
Meshelemiah had seven sons: Zechariah his firstborn, Jediael the second, Zechariah the third, and Nethanel the fourth.
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Jedai the seventh.
Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah his firstborn, Jehozaban the second, Joah the third, Sheber the fourth, and Matlal the fifth.
Gammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth, for the Lord had blessed him.
Sons were born to his son Shemaiah who ruled over their ancestral house, because they were mighty men.
The sons of Shemaiah: Gathiel, Gedahiel, Obediel, and Zechariah, mighty warriors; Eliah and Semachiah.
All these were descendants of Obed-Edom. They, their sons, and their brothers were mighty men, capable of the work of the sanctuary: sixty-two descendants of Obed-Edom.
Meshelemiah, his eldest son, had eighteen sons who were mighty warriors.
Hosah, from the sons of Merari, had sons who were mighty men. His eldest son had died, so his father appointed the next one as chief, but did not give him the title of firstborn.
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen.
The gates were assigned individually to these men, with guard duties corresponding to those of their brothers, so that they could serve in the sanctuary.
They cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their ancestral households, for each gate.
The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. They cast lots for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and his lot came out for the north.
To Obed-edom fell the south, and to his sons the house of the thresholds.
To Shuppim and Hosah fell the west, as far as the gate situated on the ascending road, guard post opposite guard post.
On the east, six Levites; on the east, four each day; on the south, four each day; and at the gatehouse, two.
At Parbar on the west, four at the roads and two at Parbar.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers from the descendants of Korah and the descendants of Merari.
Among the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the sacred things.
The descendants of Ladan, from the descendants of Gershon belonging to Ladan—the heads of ancestral families belonging to Ladan the Gershonite—were Nahli.
The sons of Nahli, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
As for the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
Samuel son of Gershon, son of Moses, was appointed over the treasuries.
As for his brother Eliezer: Rehabiah was his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

This Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the sacred gifts dedicated by King David, the heads of ancestral families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders.
From warfare and from plunder they dedicated things to strengthen the house of the Lord.
Everything dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah, and everything else that was dedicated, was entrusted to Shelomith and his brothers.
Among the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to duties outside the temple, serving as officials and judges over Israel.
Among the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, were in charge of the census of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the work of the Lord and the service of the king.

Among the Hebronites, Neriah was the head of the Hebronites according to their genealogies and ancestral families. In the fortieth year of David's reign they were sought out, and mighty warriors were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.

His relatives were 2,700 capable men, heads of ancestral families. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in every matter concerning God and the king.

The Israelites, according to their numbers—the heads of ancestral families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers—served the king in every matter concerning the divisions that came on duty and went off duty month by month throughout all the months of the year. Each division numbered 24,000.
Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel. His division numbered 24,000.
He was one of the descendants of Perez and was chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
Over the division for the second month was David the Hohite, with his division and Mikloth as leader. His division numbered 24,000.
The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the chief priest. His division numbered 24,000.
This Benaiah was a warrior among the Thirty and was in command of the Thirty. His son Mizbar was over his division.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel, Joab's brother, and after him his son Zabdiel. His division numbered 24,000.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Nazrahite. His division numbered 24,000.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division numbered 24,000.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the descendants of Ephraim. His division numbered 24,000.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the family of Zerah. His division numbered 24,000.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, from the family of Benjamin. His division numbered 24,000.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, from the family of Zerah. His division numbered 24,000.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, from the descendants of Ephraim. His division numbered 24,000.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, from the family of Othniel. His division numbered 24,000.
Over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer son of Zichri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah.
For Levi: Hashabiah son of Mekuel. For Aaron: Zadok.
For Judah: Elihu, one of David’s brothers. For Issachar: Omri son of Michael.
Over Zebulun was Shemaiah son of Obadiah; over Naphtali was Jeremoth son of Azriel.
Over the descendants of Ephraim was Hoshea son of Azariah; over the half-tribe of Manasseh was Joel son of Periah.
Over the half of Manasseh in Gilead was Iddo son of Zechariah; over Benjamin was Jaasiel son of Abner.
Over Dan was Azriel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
David did not count those twenty years old and under, because the Lord had said that he would make Israel as numerous as the stars in heaven.
Joab son of Zeruiah began to count them but did not finish. Wrath came upon Israel because of this, and the total was not entered as a census in the chronicles of King David.
Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king's treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the countryside, in the towns, in the villages, and in the towers.
Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who worked in the fields, cultivating the land.
Shemaiah the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards. Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine stores.
Over the olive trees and sycamore trees in the lowland: Baal-hanan the Gederite. Over the stores of oil: Jeush.
Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the cattle grazing in Sharon. Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the cattle in the valley.
Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels. Judah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.
Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials in charge of King David’s property.
Jonathan, David's friend, was a counselor, an intelligent man and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni was with the king's sons.
Ahithophel was the king’s counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. Joab was commander of the king’s army.

David assembled all the leaders of Israel, the tribal leaders, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the king's commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, those in charge of the property and livestock belonging to the king and his sons, the trusted officials, and the mighty warriors. They all came to Jerusalem.

He said to them, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord and for the dwelling place of our God. I had prepared everything to build the house.
But the Lord said to me, 'You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a warrior and because you are a man who has shed much blood.'

The Lord, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father's family to be king over Israel forever. For he chose a king for himself from the house of Judah, and from the clan of Judah he chose my father's family for himself. From my father's family he chose me to be king over Israel.
Of all my sons—for the Lord has given me many sons—he chose Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the exalted kingdom of Israel.
He said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my house and my courts, because I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. And if he is unwilling to keep my commandments and my judgments as he does today—

Now, in the sight of all Israel, the people of the Lord, and before the Lord our God, keep and seek out his commandments. Then you will possess this land forever and ever and pass it on to your children forever and ever, and it will not be ruined.

And you, Solomon my son, know everything that the Lord our God has commanded us. Serve him wholeheartedly and willingly, not under compulsion, because the Lord knows everything in the heart and understands everything that people think in their minds. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will destroy you.
Know and see that the Lord has chosen you to build a house for the Lord’s holy name. Be strong, be courageous, and do the work.

David gave his son Solomon the plan of the porticoes and the measurements of the house, of the [?], of the upper rooms, of the inner and outer colonnades, of the upper and lower stories, of the treasury, of the service rooms of the Lord’s house, of the slaughterhouse, of the cupbearers’ room, and of the lamp room—the place where the gold lampstands were kept, with their gold lamps, their wicks, their tongs, and their oil vessels. David wrote everything down and gave it to his son Solomon: silver tables and gold tables, silver pitchers and gold pitchers, [?], forks, and silver strainers. The weight of the gold in these vessels was beyond counting.

David said to his son Solomon, “Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or terrified, because the Lord of lords is with you. He will not forsake you or abandon you until you finish all the construction work on the Lord’s house.

Look, I have put the divisions of the priests and Levites in charge of all the work of the Lord’s house. They are with you, and they are in charge of all the work of Gershon the treasurer. They will skillfully carry out all the tasks required for the work of the Lord’s house. Look, I have appointed officials and leaders over them to oversee and carry out all the work that is required.”

King David said to all the assemblies of Israel, “This Solomon, my son, is a young boy. The Lord chose him from among all my sons because he is a wise and discerning boy. This work entrusted to him is not small; it is great, because it was not entrusted for a human being. So be strong and courageous in carrying it out, because it belongs to the Lord our God.

With all my strength and all my possessions, I have prepared everything needed for the house of the Lord my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver work, bronze for the bronze work, iron for the ironwork, wood for the woodwork, cedar for the cedar work, precious stones, and pearls.
Everything needed for the house I have prepared and supplied out of my poverty. Out of my poverty I have also prepared silver for the expenses of the house of my God:
a million talents of gold, of fine gold, and two million talents of silver to overlay the walls of the house.

Where gold is needed, let gold be used, and where silver is needed, let silver be used, for all the work, so that the work may be completed in its appointed month. The work must not be delayed, but must be completed as required according to its schedule.”
The heads of the ancestral families, the leaders of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and those in charge of the king’s work gathered together.

They gave for the work of the Lord’s house five thousand talents of gold, two hundred thousand of fine tin for the pipes, twenty thousand talents of silver, seventy thousand talents of Corinthian bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
They gave silver and gold, as needed, to the treasury of the Lord’s house through Gershon the treasurer.
All the people of Israel rejoiced over all the gifts, because David had given them wholeheartedly before the Lord. David too rejoiced greatly and offered great praises to the Lord.
David blessed the Lord before all the assemblies of Israel. David said, “Blessed are you, Lord, God of Israel our father, from everlasting to everlasting.

For yours, Lord, are greatness, might, glory, beauty, splendor, and honor, because you rule in heaven and on earth. Yours, Lord, is the kingdom, and you rule over everything. Wisdom, might, and knowledge are yours.
Wealth and honor come from you, and you rule over everything. Power and might are yours, and you make great and strengthen all the creatures you have created.
Now, Lord our God, we give thanks to you and praise your great name.
For what am I, and what are my people? For I have learned from all my teachers, because your way is the way of life. You have helped me, and you are our hope, Lord our God.
For we are like steam from a pot, and we are temporary residents before you, short-lived in this world. You ruled over our ancestors long ago and instructed them in the way they should walk and live.
And we praise you, LORD our God, that you may rescue us from all who mistreat us and from the nations who insult us and say to us, “Where is your God whom you serve?”

I know, my God, that you examine the heart and delight in faithfulness. In the faithfulness of my heart I have praised all these things. And now I have seen your people who are here praising you with great joy and saying:

“LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our ancestors, keep forever all these things you have promised us. Turn our hearts away from evil so that we do not sin before you, and prepare our hearts to fear you.” I, David, responded and said this:

“LORD my God, give my son Solomon also a wholehearted heart to keep your commandments, your decrees, and your covenant, to do everything you have commanded, and to build the house for which I have made preparations, so that your great name may be held holy and praised in the world you created, before those who fear you.”

David said to all the people of Israel, “Bless the LORD your God.” And all the people blessed the LORD, the God of their ancestors. They fell down and worshiped the LORD, and they also blessed King David.

They sacrificed sacrifices before the LORD and presented burnt offerings before the LORD on the following day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with abundant drink offerings. The Israelites also offered a great many sacrifices for themselves.
They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. They established Solomon son of David as king and appointed Zadok as priest.
Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD’s kingdom to reign in place of his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the mighty warriors and all the sons of King David submitted to Solomon his son.
The LORD exalted Solomon greatly in the sight of all Israel and bestowed royal splendor on him unlike that of any of the kings of Israel who had preceded him.
David son of Jesse established Solomon his son as king over all Israel.
David reigned over all Israel for forty years. He reigned in Hebron for seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned for thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
David son of Jesse died at a good old age, old and satisfied with the days of his life. He had grown great in worldly wealth and honor, and his son Solomon reigned after him.
The deeds of David king of Israel, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the prophet, in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the records of Gad the prophet:

his entire reign, his mighty deeds, and the times that passed over him, over Israel, and over the whole kingdom of his land. For David did what was right before the LORD and did not depart from anything he commanded him throughout all the days of his life.
